subject: MSA: availability ladder & maintenance policy - proposed edits
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@stellate.io>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: David Ortiz <david.ortiz@stellate.io>
Date: 2025-05-18T21:03:00Z
Subject: MSA: availability ladder & maintenance policy - proposed edits

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier — Stellate legal reviewed the draft MSA and sent back a handful of edits focused on availability and maintenance. I've attached their redlines (Stellate_MSA_redlines_20250518.docx). Main asks summarized here so we can align before formal redline exchange: 

- Uptime target: request 99.95% monthly for the public inference API (they're uncomfortable with 99.9%).
- Service credits: they want a pro-rata ladder that starts at 0.5% credit at 99.90 and scales to 20% if uptime < 99.0%; also want a cap equal to 3 months' fees.
- Response times: P1 initial response 30 minutes (24x7), P2 4 hours, P3 24 hours.
- Maintenance windows: request no more than 2 hours/month per region, with 72-hour advance notice for planned maintenance; carveout for emergency security patches but require post-notification within 8 hours.
- Major release blackout: they want a 2-week window before major client launches where no planned maintenance occurs.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept the 99.95 target for critical endpoints, or propose a compromise? Also include any operational carveouts we need (e.g., planned capacity upgrades) so we can avoid future churn in procurement.

If helpful, David can join a short call with legal and product next week.

Best,
Laura
Procurement Manager | Stellate Analytics

Attachment: Stellate_MSA_redlines_20250518.docx (Word doc with inline edits)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@stellate.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-05-19T02:12:00Z
Subject: Re: MSA: availability ladder & maintenance policy - proposed edits

Laura — thanks for the clear summary and the redlines. We're aligned on wanting a clean, operationally realistic SLA that doesn't expose either team to unbounded credit risk. Quick responses to your asks and a proposed compromise below: 

- Uptime target: Redwood can offer 99.95% for a defined set of "critical endpoints" (inference + model selection API). For the broader control plane we propose 99.9% (same monthly measurement). We'll provide a short appendix that enumerates the critical endpoints.
- Service credits: agree on a tiered ladder but propose cap at 2 months' fees instead of 3. Also suggest a non-linear ladder: 0.5% credit at 99.90-99.84, 5% at 99.83-99.5, 15% at 99.49-99.0, 30% <99.0 — we can tune exact bands.
- Response times: P1 1 hour initial response for hosted customers by default; for Stellate (enterprise) we can commit to 30 minutes if they subscribe to the dedicated on-call add-on or select the enterprise support tier. P2/P3 as you propose (4h/24h).
- Maintenance windows: agree to target 2 hours/month per region for platform-impacting maintenance with 72-hour notice. For emergency security patches we will perform repairs outside the window but will provide incident postmortem within 8 hours of the action.
- Major release blackout: we can honor a 2-week blackout per major launch provided Stellate gives gate dates in writing at least 21 days in advance.

Next steps: I'm looping in Marissa for legal wording and Aditya for product ops implications. We'll draft a Redwood_proposal_SLA_v2.pdf that captures the compromise and specific credit math so you have something to circulate internally. Would a live 30-min sync on Tue 5/20 10:00 PT work for your team?

Thanks,
Evelyn
Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_proposal_SLA_v2.pdf (proposal summary + credit ladder)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: 2025-05-19T08:34:00Z
Subject: Re: MSA: availability ladder & maintenance policy - proposed edits

Eve/Adi — I reviewed Stellate's redlines and Evelyn's suggested compromises. I attached a legal redline (MSA_redline_marissa_v1.pdf) that incorporates the operational concessions while protecting Redwood's exposure. High-level notes for negotiation: 

- Define "Measurement Period" and ensure credits are calculated on customer invoice net of discounts; add minimum uptime measurement window to avoid minute-level noise.
- Cap: we can accept a cap but recommend limiting to the greater of two months' fees or the prepaid term for fixed-term customers — this prevents anomalous refunds for long prepaids.
- Emergency maintenance: add a clause requiring Redwood to use "commercially reasonable efforts" to avoid customer-impacting emergency work and to schedule rolling patch windows where possible; require a post-action technical summary within 48 hours (not 8) — 8 hours is operationally tight for a coordinated remediation.
- Response SLAs: keep default P1 at 1 hour in the public SLA; enterprise support tier allows 30-minute P1. We'll add an explicit statement that acknowledgements are not incident resolutions and that resolution timelines are incident-severity dependent.

I'll produce a redline with tracked language for the credit ladder math and maintenance carveouts. Note: procurement will often push for absolute uptime commitments — we should prioritize enumerating critical endpoints and attaching an appendix that limits the 99.95 promise to those endpoints.

Marissa
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: MSA_redline_marissa_v1.pdf (tracked changes - legal)

> On 2025-05-19 Evelyn wrote:
> > Laura — thanks for the clear summary and the redlines...

From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@stellate.io>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: David Ortiz <david.ortiz@stellate.io>
Date: 2025-05-20T16:45:00Z
Subject: Re: MSA: availability ladder & maintenance policy - proposed edits

Evelyn/Marissa — appreciate the quick turn. A few clarifying points from Stellate legal/procurement after reviewing Marissa's notes: 

1) Cap: Stellate prefers a flat 3-month fee cap; moving to 2-months or variable logic is a hard sell internally. If Redwood cannot accept 3 months, please propose a business justification we can present to our CFO (i.e., expected annualized cost exposure).
2) Emergency remedy post-notification: Stellate's security team insists on 8 hours for high-severity fixes to confirm mitigations and actions taken; would Redwood consider 24 hours for the post-incident operational report (Acknowledgement + initial mitigation summary within 8 hours, full remediation summary within 24)?
3) Critical endpoints appendix: agree — please circulate the appendix with endpoint URIs and measurement definitions so we can lock the scope.

We can do the quick sync Tue 5/20 at 10:00 PT — David and our legal counsel will join. If we can get a near-final redline by end of day Monday, procurement will try to move to signature in the same week.

Thanks,
Laura

Folks — quick internal recap and action items after the call: 

- Procurement wants 3-month cap. Marissa recommended 2-months or term-based floor; need a one-liner business rationale if we hold at 2-months. Aditya, can you provide an expected annualized worst-case cost estimate for Stellate profile (monthly spend ~ $65k) so we can quantify exposure?
- Product: finalize critical endpoints appendix and measurement script (Aditya). Target: publish appendix with exact URIs and probe methodology by 5/22 EOD.
- Legal: update redline to reflect 8-hour acknowledgement + 24-hour full remediation report language; clarify "commercially reasonable efforts" phrasing. (Marissa)
- Sales/CX: offer Stellate an "enterprise on-call" add-on pricing for 30-minute P1 SLA — propose $3k/mo premium. (Eve)

I'll draft the consolidated compromise and send to Stellate with a DocuSign link once legal finishes the redline.

Eve

Date: 2025-05-23T16:12:00Z
Subject: Final compromise proposal and next steps (DocuSign link)

Laura — thanks for the productive discussion earlier this week. Attached is Redwood's consolidated compromise (Redwood_proposal_SLA_v2.pdf) which incorporates: 

- 99.95% monthly uptime for enumerated critical endpoints (appendix attached), 99.9% for the remainder of the control plane.
- Service credit ladder (non-linear) with a cap equal to the greater of two months' fees or prepaid term; we included a short sensitivity table showing Stellate's exposure at current spend levels.
- Incident reporting: acknowledgement and initial mitigation summary within 8 hours for high-severity events; full remediation report within 24 hours.
- Maintenance: 2 hours/month per region, 72-hour notice; emergency patches allowed with post-action report. Major-release blackout honored with 21-day advance gate notice.
- Enterprise add-on: 30-minute P1 initial response available at $3,000/mo.

If Stellate agrees with the language in the attached PDF, I've created a DocuSign envelope to streamline signatures: https://www.docusign.com/prepare/abcdef-12345-stellate-msa. Please let me know if legal needs further edits; Marissa is standing by for one more pass.

Looking forward — if procurement signs off we can schedule onboarding and runbook handoff next week.

Best,
Evelyn
Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_proposal_SLA_v2.pdf; MSA_redline_marissa_v1.pdf
